fullText.simplified:
第二十七章、星河地图

    石文谦和简西跌入到洞底。他们时刻保持着警惕，摸索着前进。可能由于之前被雨淋湿了，两个人偶尔能听到水滴到石块上的声音，偶尔还能听到一些奇怪的声音从远处传来。像是石块滑动的声音，又像是地下暗流的流动声。忽然，一阵冷风无声无息地从古道的深处涌来，仿佛来自地宫最深处的呼吸。
    “文……文谦。”简西紧张地抓住了石文谦的衣服，“你说，我们这样一直往前走，会到哪里啊？会到秦始皇的地宫吗？”
    “哪有那么容易，而且进去也是相当危险的，能不能活着出来都不知道。我读过《史记·秦始皇本纪》，里面描写了秦始皇的地宫设计和构造，‘以水银为百川江河大海，机相灌输，上具天文，下具地理。’”石文谦说了一句古书里的原文，让简西没太听懂。
    “什么意思？”简西困惑地问道。
    石文谦回想起自己当年读到这段文字时，他也觉得不可思议。仔细分析，这句话的意思大概是这样的：
    “以水银为百川江河大海”是说秦始皇陵的地宫中，用水银模拟了中国江河湖海的景象。多少水银呢？100吨水银，这是现代地质勘测仪器探测得出的数据。主陵墓区域的水银含量超标，远远高于正常水平，而且东北方水银最多，南方少一些，西北方最弱。这符合秦帝国的水系版图。秦朝的时候，中国的东北方是大海，南方有大江和湖泊，西北缺水少雨。
    “机相灌输”里的“机”是指机关装置或技术手段，“灌输”是指流动。整句话意思是通过某种机关系统来控制水银的流动。也就是说地宫中的水银并不是静止的，而是通过装置来模拟流水的效果。
    “上具天文”指的是墓室顶部装饰有象征天空和天文现象的图案，“下具地理”则意味着墓室底部有象征地理和大地的布局。
    那装有秦始皇的棺椁又在哪里呢？据说，棺椁漂浮在水银上。准确来说，棺椁是漂浮在水银打造的秦帝国之中。这让秦始皇在死后世界，也能真实地感受到属于他的秦帝国。这是他打下来的江山，他要全部带走，甚至天上的星象与地下的山河他都要带到他的地宫中，继续统治他的帝国。
fullText.traditional:
第二十七章、星河地圖

    石文謙和簡西跌入到洞底。他們時刻保持著警惕，摸索著前進。可能由於之前被雨淋濕了，兩個人偶爾能聽到水滴到石塊上的聲音，偶爾還能聽到一些奇怪的聲音從遠處傳來。像是石塊滑動的聲音，又像是地下暗流的流動聲。忽然，一陣冷風無聲無息地從古道的深處湧來，彷彿來自地宮最深處的呼吸。
    “文……文謙。”簡西緊張地抓住了石文謙的衣服，“你說，我們這樣一直往前走，會到哪裡啊？會到秦始皇的地宮嗎？”
    “哪有那麼容易，而且進去也是相當危險的，能不能活著出來都不知道。我讀過《史記·秦始皇本紀》，裡面描寫了秦始皇的地宮設計和構造，‘以水銀為百川江河大海，機相灌輸，上具天文，下具地理。’”石文謙說了一句古書裡的原文，讓簡西沒太聽懂。
    “什麼意思？”簡西困惑地問道。
    石文謙回想起自己當年讀到這段文字時，他也覺得不可思議。仔細分析，這句話的意思大概是這樣的：
    “以水銀為百川江河大海”是說秦始皇陵的地宮中，用水銀模擬了中國江河湖海的景象。多少水銀呢？100噸水銀，這是現代地質勘測儀器探測得出的數據。主陵墓區域的水銀含量超標，遠遠高於正常水平，而且東北方水銀最多，南方少一些，西北方最弱。這符合秦帝國的水系版圖。秦朝的時候，中國的東北方是大海，南方有大江和湖泊，西北缺水少雨。
    “機相灌輸”裡的“機”是指機關裝置或技術手段，“灌輸”是指流動。整句話意思是通過某種機關系統來控制水銀的流動。也就是說地宮中的水銀並不是靜止的，而是通過裝置來模擬流水的效果。
    “上具天文”指的是墓室頂部裝飾有象徵天空和天文現象的圖案，“下具地理”則意味著墓室底部有象徵地理和大地的佈局。
    那裝有秦始皇的棺槨又在哪裡呢？據說，棺槨漂浮在水銀上。準確來說，棺槨是漂浮在水銀打造的秦帝國之中。這讓秦始皇在死後世界，也能真實地感受到屬於他的秦帝國。這是他打下來的江山，他要全部帶走，甚至天上的星象與地下的山河他都要帶到他的地宮中，繼續統治他的帝國。

sentences.simplified: 这是他打下来的江山，他要全部带走，
sentences.traditional: 這是他打下來的江山，他要全部帶走，
sentences.pinyin: zhè shì tā dǎ xià lai de jiāng shān tā yào quán bù dài zǒu
sentences.english: This was the kingdom that he built, and he wanted to take it all with him.

sentences.simplified: 甚至天上的星象与地下的山河他都要带到他的地宫中，
sentences.traditional: 甚至天上的星象與地下的山河他都要帶到他的地宮中，
sentences.pinyin: shèn zhì tiān shàng de xīng xiàng yǔ dì xià de shān hé tā dōu yào dài dào tā de dì gōng zhōng
sentences.english: Even the stars in the sky and the mountains and rivers on the earth, he wanted to bring them all into his underground palace, ..

sentences.simplified: 继续统治他的帝国。
sentences.traditional: 繼續統治他的帝國。
sentences.pinyin: jì xù tǒng zhì tā de dì guó
sentences.english: .. so he could continue to rule his empire.

sentence_translations: Chapter 27: Map of the Stars
Shi Wenqian and Jian Xi fell to the bottom of the pit. They remained vigilant at all times, feeling their way forward.
Perhaps due to being soaked by the rain earlier, the two of them could sometimes hear the sound of water dripping onto the stones, ..
.. and sometimes they could also hear some strange noises coming from afar.
It sounded like the noise of stones sliding, and also like the flow of a hidden, underground current.
Suddenly, a cold wind silently surged from the depths of the ancient path, ..
.. as if it were breathing from the deepest part of the underground palace.
“Wen … Wenqian,” Jian Xi nervously grabbed Shi Wenqian’s clothes.
“Tell me, if we keep going forward like this, where will we end up? Will we end up at the underground palace of Qin Shi Huang?”
“It’s not that easy, and it is quite dangerous to go in. We don’t even know if we can make it out alive.
I have read ‘Records of the Grand Historian: The Annals of Qin Shi Huang’, ..
.. which describes the design and structure of Qin Shi Huang’s underground palace:
‘Mercury was used to create the hundred rivers, the Yellow River and the Yangtze, and the seas, with mechanisms to control the flow.
Above, there were celestial bodies, and below, the landscape of the earth.’”
Shi Wenqian quoted a passage from an ancient text, which Jian Xi didn’t quite understand.
“What does it mean?” Jian Xi asked, puzzled.
Shi Wenqian recalled how he had found this passage unfathomable when he first read it back then.
Breaking it down carefully, the meaning of these sentences is roughly as follows:
“Mercury was used to create the hundred rivers, the Yellow River and the Yangtze, and the seas” ..
.. means that in the underground palace of the Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang, ..
.. mercury was used to simulate the landscapes of China’s rivers, lakes, and seas.
How much mercury? One hundred tons of mercury. This is data obtained from modern geological survey instruments.
The mercury content in the main burial area exceeds the standard, far above normal levels, ..
.. with the highest concentration in the northeast, somewhat less in the south, and the weakest in the northwest.
This aligns with the water system map of the Qin Empire.
During the Qin Dynasty, ..
.. the northeast of China had a great sea, the south had large rivers and lakes, while the northwest was arid and lacked rainfall.
In “with mechanisms to control the flow”, “机” refers to mechanical devices or technical means, and “灌输” means to flow.
The entire sentence means to control the flow of mercury through a certain system of mechanisms.
In other words, the mercury in the underground palace is not static, ..
.. but rather flows through a system to simulate the effect of running water.
“Above, there were celestial bodies” ..
.. indicating that the ceiling of the burial chamber is adorned with patterns that symbolize the sky and astronomical phenomena.
“Below, the landscape of the earth” ..
.. means that the floor of the burial chamber has arrangements symbolizing geographical features and the earth.
So, where is the coffin that contains Qin Shi Huang? It is said that the coffin floats on mercury.
To be precise, the coffin floats on the mercury that represents the Qin Empire.
This allows Qin Shi Huang to truly experience the Qin Empire that belongs to him, even in the world after death.
This was the kingdom that he built, and he wanted to take it all with him.
Even the stars in the sky and the mountains and rivers on the earth, he wanted to bring them all into his underground palace, ..
.. so he could continue to rule his empire.
